Student-t likelihood between data and model prediction

Source: R/objClass.R
normT.Rd

Builds the objective of a fit whose residuals follow a Student-t distribution with df degrees of freedom and scale given by the error model or the data's sigma: the -2 log likelihood of the data, summed over the conditions. The tails are heavier than those of normL2(), so single outliers move the fit less; the limit of large df is normL2().

Usage

normT(
  data,
  x,
  errmodel = NULL,
  df,
  times = NULL,
  attrName = "data",
  optBLOQ = c("M3", "M1")
)

Arguments

data

Object of class datalist. Each condition of the data has to be a condition of x.

x

Object of class prdfn.

errmodel

Optional object of class obsfn. The error model may be defined only for a subset of conditions.

df

Degrees of freedom, a positive finite number, fixed during the fit.

times

Optional time points at which the prediction is evaluated in addition to the data times: a numeric vector for all conditions, which then share one grid, or a list named by condition, which gives each condition a separate grid. The prediction of a condition starts at the first time of the grid, where the initial values take effect, so a single time per condition sets the start of that condition. A model built with odemodel(..., includeTimeZero = TRUE), the default, has 0 in every grid and so starts at 0 at the latest. Fixed-time events before the start do not fire. Event times should be included if the model uses events.

attrName

Character string. The objective value is additionally returned as an attribute of this name, and the sum of squares behind it under chi2. Adding objectives pools the terms sharing an attrName, so chi2 stays one number; where two attrNames meet it splits into chi2_<attrName> per contribution.

optBLOQ

"M3" (default, the probability of lying below the limit under the t distribution) or "M1" (censored rows dropped).

Value

An objective function of class objfn, as normL2() returns it, usable in trust(), mstrust(), profile() and em().

See also

normL2()

Examples

## A straight line with two gross outliers: the Student-t fit stays on the line
x <- Xd(data.frame(name = "y", time = 0:9, row.names = paste0("a", 0:9)), condition = "C1")
set.seed(1)
y <- 1 + 0.5 * (0:9) + rnorm(10, 0, 0.1)
y[c(3, 8)] <- y[c(3, 8)] + c(3, -4)
data <- as.datalist(data.frame(name = "y", time = 0:9, value = y, sigma = 0.1, condition = "C1"))
pars <- setNames(1 + 0.5 * (0:9), paste0("a", 0:9))
obj <- normT(data, x, df = 3)
obj(pars)$value
#> [1] 26.33673
